Her days were filled with happiness. She was not rich, she had no amazing skills, but she was happy in life.

It was a miracle she was born into this world. Her mother had an abortion before her, and the fact that she was even born seemed like a marvel.

Her childhood had been fantastic, days spent with her mother, father, and brother teemed with vivid memories of flowers and hikes, sleepovers and birthday parties.

Her teenage years, her friends, her first love, her first heartbreak, she was happy through the good and the bad. She was a ray of sunshine in a world of darkness.

Then one day everything broke apart. All of her memories were false, everything she ever knew had been a lie, and it dawned on her in one moment.

"Had I been in this asylum my whole life?" She softly spoke to herself.

She gazed around her seeing that everyone else was in white scrubs, moping around the linoleum floors, heads down, fluorescent lighting above. "This is your sacrifice," a voice intoned. "Your mother is right next to you, look." Said that voice inside her mind.

Down the hall she heard the laughter of one of the patients.

She looked to her right to see the woman whom she though was her mother. "What the fuck is going on?" Panic spreading, fear hung upon her like an extra set of clothing, wrapping her in cold. She felt like she was moving through water, could barely pull in another breath.

This must be a dream, she though to herself. Wake up! Wake up!

There was no waking.

There was only sacrifice.

And then she forgot her past.

And she was one of them.
